title: C++ Introduction
summary: Meet C++ with three short programs. Print a friendly message, add two counts and make a choice with an if statement.
introduction: C++ is a language for writing computer programs. It is used in games and many other tools. A compiler turns your code into a program. Think of the code as a recipe and the computer as the cook: each line gives it a step to follow.
learningObjectives: Explain why C++ code needs a compiler
Print text and add whole numbers
Choose a step with an if statement

rows: A tool that turns C++ code into a program.
A name for a stored value.
A tool that sends values to the terminal.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/cpp/setup) to use C++ on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
iostream gives the program tools for input and output. main is the starting point. std::cout sends the text to the terminal.
int holds a whole number. The braces give the starting value. The plus sign adds the two values.

blocks.title: pencils.cpp

blocks.text: The >= sign means at least. The if block runs because the score is at least 5. Try a score of 2 to see the difference.

blocks.title: score.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: Save C++ examples as .cpp files. Use a C++ compiler such as g++, not the C compiler command from another tutorial.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change the greeting to your name. Next, change the two pencil counts and predict their total.
